geminiPrice: Gemini priced at $1.50 per million input tokens and $9.00 per million output + thinking tokens (Google Cloud's published 'Global' price for Gemini 3.5 Flash, Oct 2026; ai.google.dev was blocked from here, so the Gemini API's own page wasn't checked). Gemini actually served gemini-3.6-flash, which the same price list shows at an introductory $0.75 / $3.75 until 31 Dec 2026, so the real bill is likely about half of what is shown. Treat these as upper-bound estimates.

findings: GOAL C3 (build under $0.50, hint under $0.01): no real Claude call ran, so there is no real lesson-build or hint cost yet. The about-me fixture is hand-written, so it has no cost data at all; it only gives the estimate shown above.

Reading one 19-24 minute video with Gemini (low resolution) cost $0.22-$0.29 (average $0.25, upper-bound price). That is part of a video lesson's build, so it leaves about $0.25 of the $0.50 budget for the Opus steps call (projection, not measured).

The 3 videos were picked as beginner HTML/CSS step-by-step builds; youtube.com is blocked here, so view counts and captions couldn't be checked. Gemini read two titles differently from the ones noted when picking them ("HTML Tutorial for Beginners - Full Course", "How to Code Your FIRST Website (in 10 minutes)"); the report shows what Gemini read.

Found by this test: in wzWmZYi4qMg's real notes Gemini escaped the code twice (every line break arrived as a typed \\n, so each file was one long line). src/learn/gemini.ts now turns that back into real lines (unescapeCode); without it that video's lesson would have been built from 11 one-line code blobs.

promptChanges.change: No code comments in the finished site.
promptChanges.why: Every line is typed by the student; comments are lines typed for nothing and inflate the estimate.

promptChanges.change: 3-10 non-blank lines, never more than 10; split long parts.
promptChanges.why: A4 / grader 'stepSize'. Now also enforced in code: steps over 12 lines are sent back.

promptChanges.change: Explicit teaching order: skeleton, then HTML content, then CSS, then JS; one new idea per step.
'watch' steps add no code; every line of the finished project is typed in some learner step.
promptChanges.why: A4 '🤖 steps are only setup'; grader 'whoTypes'. Enforced in code too.

promptChanges.change: Instructions say what to add and where in words, for a 14-year-old who never coded.
Each hint stronger: words only, then the spot + tag name, then part of the code with … gaps; hint 3 never the whole 'expected'.
promptChanges.why: A6. Enforced in code: a hint 3 holding the whole answer is sent back.
